title: Left unitality of normalized scalar extension
statement: Let \(A,B\) be commutative rings, \(\varphi:A\to B\) a unital ring map, and \(T\) a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. In the ordinary unbounded derived categories of small-etale module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], let \(Q:D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to D(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)\), \(\delta:Q(K\otimes L)\simeq QK\otimes QL\), and \(e:Q1_A\simeq1_B\) be the normalized scalar extension, tensor, and unit comparisons [def-pur-exceptional-coefficient-normalizations]. Then for every \(K\), \(\delta_{1_A,K};(e\mathbin{\triangleright}QK);\lambda_{QK}=Q(\lambda_K)\). Semicolon denotes composition in application order. The predicate SiteScalarLeftUnitLaw is this equation with the site's monoidal parameters shared.

proof.text: Apply leftUnit_on_representative to the normalized ordinary sheaf scalar functor and its derived adjoint representative. Its tensor and unit squares are the defining normalizations, and the representative at a K-flat complex is invertible. Both paths are natural transformations. Localization extensionality and a flat K-flat resolution of each complex extend the equality from these representatives to all derived objects. The chosen site tensor comparison equals the raw uniquely normalized one.

    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B)
